steps.claim: From i to i + 1 (ih: the claim at stage i), for a basis index k with j ≤ floorOf(k) + i + 1 or level(k) ≤ ϱ: split on whether k already satisfies the condition of stage i.
If j ≤ floorOf(k) + i or level(k) ≤ ϱ, then X_{mk} ∈ B^S_{d+(c+3)i} ⊂ B^S_{d+(c+3)(i+1)} by ih and monotonicity.

steps.claim: Otherwise floorOf(k) + i + 1 = j and level(k) > ϱ, so k = e*_a with a = floorOf(k) < j; h gives w with w(e*_b) = δ_{ab} (b ≤ a), w ∈ vecsOfSize(S, c), Xw ∈ vecsOfSize(S, d). Then X_{mk} = (Xw)_m − X_m·(w − 1_k), 1_k the k-th standard vector: (Xw)_m ∈ B^S_d ⊂ B^S_{d+(c+3)i+c+2}; w − 1_k has entries in B^S_{c+1} and vanishes at every e*_b with b ≤ a, so wherever it is nonzero the index k' has level(k') ≤ ϱ or is e*_b with b > a, hence satisfies the condition of stage i and X_{mk'} ∈ B^S_{d+(c+3)i} by ih; the dot product lies in B^S_{d+(c+3)i+c+2} and the difference in B^S_{d+(c+3)(i+1)}.
